implementation_notes: Rust has the strongest legitimate case in this catalogue and also the strongest temptation. The legitimate case: `unsafe` with a documented invariant, `get_unchecked`, SIMD intrinsics, and `#[repr(C)]` layouts for FFI or hardware registers are all real engineering when a profile justifies them, and Rust's `unsafe` keyword is exactly the mechanism for making the cost and the obligation explicit. The premature case is using `unsafe` for speed before profiling, which gives up memory safety for a gain that was never measured. The second is bounds-check elision by index gymnastics (`while i < v.len() { x = v[i]; ... }` restructured into unsafe pointers) in code that runs once.
idiom_name: unsafe blocks added for speed; bounds-check elision by index gymnastics
pitfalls: `unsafe` blocks introduced for speed before a profile, giving up memory safety for an unverified gain.
Manual bounds-check elision by index arithmetic in code that runs once.
SIMD intrinsics written before checking whether the compiler already vectorises the loop.
`#[inline(always)]` added to a large function, increasing code size and defeating the optimiser's own heuristics.
